_about: Spark Word bank. Each word: a kid-friendly definition (10 words or fewer), a one-line tip for how the parent introduces it, and a picture once one is made in Canva (null until then). Words are useful 'Tier 2' words children will meet again in books. Review every entry before launch.

words.definition: Very, very big.
words.introTip: Stretch your arms as wide as they go and whisper, "enormous!" Ask what else is enormous.

words.definition: Very, very old, from long ago.
words.introTip: Talk about something old in your family, then say dinosaurs are even older: ancient.

words.definition: Old bones or shapes turned into stone.
words.introTip: Press a hand into play dough and say a fossil is a shape left behind long ago.

words.definition: To step down hard and loud.
words.introTip: Stomp your feet together three times. Quiet steps are not stomps!

words.definition: Wild and strong, not afraid of anything.
words.introTip: Make your fiercest face together, then your gentlest face.

words.definition: An animal that hunts other animals for food.
words.introTip: Name a predator together, like a wolf or a shark, and what it hunts.

words.definition: Gone forever; none are left alive.
words.introTip: Explain that dinosaurs are extinct, so we only see their bones now.

words.definition: Soft and careful, not rough.
words.introTip: Pat your child's hand gently, then show how you'd pat a kitten.

words.definition: A hole or tunnel an animal digs to live in.
words.introTip: Burrow under a blanket together like a rabbit in its burrow.

words.definition: Always sticking by your friend.
words.introTip: Say a dog is loyal because it always comes back to you. Who is loyal to you?

words.definition: To rub gently with a nose.
words.introTip: Nuzzle your child's cheek like a pony would.

words.definition: The home where an animal or plant lives.
words.introTip: Ask: a fish's habitat is water. What is a bird's habitat?

words.definition: To sneak around quietly, looking for something.
words.introTip: Prowl across the room on tiptoe like a cat.

words.definition: To move with quick little steps.
words.introTip: Scurry your fingers up your child's arm like a beetle.

words.definition: A feeler on a bug's head.
words.introTip: Hold two fingers up on your head and wiggle them like antennae.

words.definition: A big group of animals living together.
words.introTip: Say ants live in a colony, like a giant family in one home.

words.definition: To flap quickly and lightly.
words.introTip: Flutter your hands like butterfly wings.

words.definition: To move slowly and quietly.
words.introTip: Creep your fingers slowly across the blanket.

words.definition: To change into something very different.
words.introTip: Say a caterpillar transforms into a butterfly. What would you transform into?

words.definition: A small, shaky light.
words.introTip: Wiggle your fingers like light glimmering on water.

words.definition: Water moving strongly in one direction.
words.introTip: Sweep your arm across like a current pushing a little boat.

words.definition: To float along slowly.
words.introTip: Drift your hand down slowly like a leaf on water.

words.definition: To jump or dive down fast.
words.introTip: Pretend to plunge into a pool: one, two, three, splash!

words.definition: Colourful sea rock that tiny animals build.
words.introTip: Say coral looks like underwater flowers, but tiny animals built it.

words.definition: To shine with a soft, wavy light.
words.introTip: Move a spoon in the light and watch it shimmer.

words.definition: To travel around and around something.
words.introTip: Walk in a circle around your child: you are orbiting them!

words.definition: To send something up and away.
words.introTip: Count down from five and launch your arms up like a rocket.

words.definition: The pull that makes things fall down.
words.introTip: Drop a sock: gravity pulled it down!

words.definition: Very far away.
words.introTip: Point out the window at something distant, then something close.

words.definition: To look around a new place to learn.
words.introTip: Ask: if you could explore anywhere, where would you go?

words.definition: A person who travels into space.
words.introTip: Pretend to float like an astronaut with no gravity.

words.definition: To shine with tiny flashes of light.
words.introTip: Open and close your fingers fast to make sparkles.

words.definition: Filled with wonder, like in a fairy tale.
words.introTip: Whisper it in a dreamy voice: an enchanted forest.

words.definition: Moving in a smooth, lovely way.
words.introTip: Wave your arm gracefully like a dancer.

words.definition: Something you hope will happen.
words.introTip: Close your eyes and each make a quiet wish.

words.definition: Easy to break; needs gentle hands.
words.introTip: Hold an imaginary bubble very delicately so it doesn't pop.

words.definition: A big field of grass and flowers.
words.introTip: Imagine lying in a meadow. What can you smell?

words.definition: Doing something even when you feel scared.
words.introTip: Remember a time your child was brave and tell them about it.

words.definition: A long trip to find something important.
words.introTip: Say your quest tonight is to find the Spark Words!

words.definition: A tall, narrow building or part of a castle.
words.introTip: Stack your fists one on top of the other to build a tower.

words.definition: Hard metal clothes that keep a knight safe.
words.introTip: Knock gently on your child's chest: clank, clank, armour!

words.definition: To keep someone or something safe.
words.introTip: Stand like a guard by the door, very serious.

words.definition: Small hard pieces covering a dragon or fish.
words.introTip: Draw tiny scales on your child's arm with your finger.

words.definition: To save someone from danger.
words.introTip: Rescue a stuffed animal from under the pillow.

words.definition: Very strong and powerful.
words.introTip: Flex your mightiest muscles together.

words.definition: Not able to be seen.
words.introTip: Hold out an invisible cookie. Can you see it? No, it's invisible!

words.definition: To fly down fast through the air.
words.introTip: Swoop your hand down like an eagle.

words.definition: Being brave inside when things are hard.
words.introTip: Put your hand on your heart: that's where courage lives.

words.definition: To keep someone safe from harm.
words.introTip: Ask: who protects you? Who do you protect?

words.definition: A long, low, shaking sound.
words.introTip: Make a deep rumble in your throat like a big truck.

words.definition: To pull or carry something heavy.
words.introTip: Haul your child onto your lap with a big heave.

words.definition: A long trip from one place to another.
words.introTip: Talk about the longest journey you have taken together.

words.definition: To make something go the way you want.
words.introTip: Hold an imaginary wheel and steer left, then right.

words.definition: A sign that tells someone what to do.
words.introTip: Show your clap signal: that's our signal for Spark Words!

words.definition: Things a truck, train or ship carries.
words.introTip: Pile pillows on your lap: this is your cargo.

words.definition: Doing something again and again to get better.
words.introTip: Say reading every night is practice, like hockey practice.

words.definition: Winning a game or a contest.
words.introTip: Throw your arms up for a victory cheer.

words.definition: Someone on the same team as you.
words.introTip: Say: tonight we're teammates for the Spark Word hunt.

words.definition: To run somewhere very fast.
words.introTip: Pretend to dash in place for three seconds.

words.definition: Not giving up, even when it's hard.
words.introTip: Make a determined face and say, "I won't give up!"

words.definition: To move smoothly, like skating on ice.
words.introTip: Glide your hand across the blanket like a skater.

words.definition: A beat that repeats, like in music.
words.introTip: Tap a rhythm on your knees and have your child copy it.

words.definition: The tune of a song you can hum.
words.introTip: Hum a favourite song: that's the melody.

words.definition: To spin around quickly.
words.introTip: Twirl one finger round and round.

words.definition: The people watching a show.
words.introTip: Clap like an audience at a concert.

words.definition: A sound that bounces back to you.
words.introTip: Say a word and have your child echo it back softly.

words.definition: To make something new.
words.introTip: Ask: what would you like to create tomorrow?

words.definition: Bright and full of colour.
words.introTip: Find the most vibrant colour in the room.

words.definition: A quick, simple drawing.
words.introTip: Sketch a tiny house on your child's palm with your finger.

words.definition: A very special piece of work.
words.introTip: Remember something your child made and call it a masterpiece.

words.definition: To make a picture in your mind.
words.introTip: Close your eyes and imagine a purple elephant.

words.definition: Tasting very, very good.
words.introTip: Rub your tummy and say "delicious" about a favourite food.

words.definition: One of the things you mix to make food.
words.introTip: Name the ingredients in pancakes together.

words.definition: To drop tiny bits over something.
words.introTip: Sprinkle pretend sugar over your child's head.

words.definition: Steps that tell you how to make food.
words.introTip: Say a recipe is like a map for cooking.

words.definition: A nice smell.
words.introTip: Sniff the air: what aroma would you love to smell right now?

words.definition: To walk around slowly with no plan.
words.introTip: Wander your fingers lazily across the pillow.

words.definition: Calm and quiet.
words.introTip: Take one slow, peaceful breath together.

words.definition: A path through woods or fields.
words.introTip: Trace a trail with your finger down your child's arm.

words.definition: A small outdoor fire for warmth and cooking.
words.introTip: Hold your hands out to a pretend campfire to warm them.

words.definition: A soft, crackly sound like moving leaves.
words.introTip: Rustle the bedsheet softly.

words.definition: To find something for the first time.
words.introTip: Say: tonight you'll discover three new words!

words.definition: A soft, gentle wind.
words.introTip: Blow a gentle breeze on your child's face.

words.definition: A big snowstorm with strong wind.
words.introTip: Wiggle all your fingers fast like snow in a blizzard.

words.definition: Very light rain.
words.introTip: Tap your fingertips lightly on the blanket like drizzle.

words.definition: Very cold and icy.
words.introTip: Shiver and say "frosty!" like a winter morning.

words.definition: Warm, soft and comfortable.
words.introTip: Snuggle up: this is cozy.

words.definition: To make something no one has made before.
words.introTip: Ask: if you could invent a machine, what would it do?

words.definition: Strong and hard to break.
words.introTip: Knock on the headboard: it's sturdy.

words.definition: A small, clever machine or tool.
words.introTip: Name a gadget in your house, like a can opener.

words.definition: To build something by putting parts together.
words.introTip: Stack two pillows: you constructed a fort!

words.definition: A drawing that shows how to build something.
words.introTip: Draw a pretend blueprint in the air.

words.definition: To pick crops when they are ready.
words.introTip: Pretend to harvest apples from a tree.

words.definition: A baby plant just starting to grow.
words.introTip: Curl up small, then slowly sprout up tall.

words.definition: A building where horses live.
words.introTip: Say a horse sleeps in a stable like you sleep in your room.

words.definition: To run fast, like a horse.
words.introTip: Gallop your hands on your knees: clip-clop, clip-clop!

words.definition: Round and full.
words.introTip: Puff out your cheeks to look plump.

words.definition: Wanting to know or learn about something.
words.introTip: Say: when you ask lots of questions, you're curious!

words.definition: To speak very, very quietly.
words.introTip: Whisper your child's name softly.

words.definition: A small, silly laugh.
words.introTip: Have a quick giggle together.

words.definition: Feeling thankful for something.
words.introTip: Share one thing you're each grateful for today.

words.definition: Very, very tired.
words.introTip: Flop down and sigh: "I'm exhausted!"

words.definition: Something you did not expect.
words.introTip: Hide your face, then pop out: surprise!

words.definition: With each other.
words.introTip: Squeeze hands: we read together.
